# zupmxode

The goal of zupmxode is to …

## Installation

You can install the development version of zupmxode from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zupmxode")
```

## Example

This is a basic example which shows you how to solve a common problem:

``` r

library(zupmxode)
## basic example code
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`add()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/add.md)
  [`prop()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/add.md)
  [`lnorm()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/add.md) :
  Residual error models
- [`pmx_ode_events()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_events.md)
  : Build an event table
- [`pmx_ode_info()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_info.md)
  : What a model is and how it is solved
- [`pmx_ode_method()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_method.md)
  : The solver of a model
- [`pmx_ode_model()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_model.md)
  : Compile a model
- [`pmx_ode_sim()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_sim.md)
  : Simulate a population
- [`pmx_ode_solve()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_solve.md)
  : Solve a model for one or more subjects
- [`pmx_ode_threads()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_threads.md)
  : The number of threads a solve uses
- [`pmx_ode_tier()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupmxode/reference/pmx_ode_tier.md)
  : The execution tier of a model
